text: First-level thinking says, 'It's a good company; let's buy the stock.' Second-level thinking says, 'It's a good company, but everyone thinks it's a great company, and it's not. So the stock is overrated and overpriced; let's sell.'
source: Howard Marks — The Most Important Thing
author: Howard Marks

text: Risk is not volatility; volatility is just the temporary fluctuation of prices. Real risk is the probability of a permanent loss of capital, which occurs when an investor overpays for an asset or is forced to sell at the bottom.
source: Howard Marks — The Most Important Thing
author: Howard Marks

text: The market is a pendulum that forever swings between unsustainable optimism (which makes stocks too expensive) and unjustified pessimism (which makes them too cheap). The intelligent investor must act contrary to these emotional swings.
source: Howard Marks — Mastering the Market Cycle
author: Howard Marks

text: You can't do the same things others do and expect to outperform. To achieve superior investment results, you must hold non-consensus views regarding value, and they must be accurate.
source: Howard Marks — The Most Important Thing
author: Howard Marks

text: Defensive investing requires ensuring that your portfolio can survive adverse outcomes. It is more important to ensure survival under negative scenarios than it is to maximize returns under positive ones.
source: Howard Marks — The Most Important Thing
author: Howard Marks
